attempts.note: Warren truss with 8 bottom nodes at y=-2.90 (just above the clearance edge), alternating diagonals, verticals at odd deck nodes, and chord/diagonal sizes graded to the midspan moment and end shear envelopes.
Attempt 1 Warren truss kept; only top-chord members D4-D5 and D5-D6 downsized from CHS219.1x8 to CHS193.7x8 to trim mass while keeping utilisation near 0.83.

Attempt 2 Warren truss kept; only the lightly loaded diagonal D0-B1 is downsized from CHS168.3x6.3 to CHS139.7x6.3 (tension util about 0.77, never in compression), trimming mass with no change to geometry or the critical chords.

Attempt 3 Warren truss kept; only the two midspan bottom-chord members B3-B4 and B4-B5 are downsized from CHS219.1x8 to CHS193.7x8 (tension about 950 kN, utilisation about 0.86 nominal, 0.93 with weakest steel), trimming about 35 kg.

Attempt 4 Warren truss with the zero-force even bottom nodes B2, B4, B6, B8 and their verticals removed (bottom chords merged into 7.07 m segments at the same sizes), end deck member D8-D9 reduced to CHS48.3x3.2 and end vertical D9-S2 to CHS88.9x5.

Attempt 5 Warren truss with top chord D6-D7 and D7-D8 downsized from CHS193.7x8 to CHS168.3x6.3 (about 637 kN compression, utilisation about 0.84 nominal, 0.91 with weakest steel), trimming about 80 kg; geometry unchanged.

Attempt 6 Warren truss with two slack members downsized: the left bottom strut S1-B1 carries only the wind reaction (about 38 kN), so it drops to CHS76.1x4, and the tension diagonal B7-D8 (about 420 kN max) drops to CHS139.7x6.3; geometry unchanged.

Resubmitting the attempt-7 Warren truss unchanged: it is the lightest design so far that holds all published cases, with worst utilisation 0.856 nominal (about 0.93 with the weakest steel) and sag 84 mm against the 106 mm limit.
